facts.claim: As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: the procedure is the request for and celebration of a civil marriage before the authorities of the Registro Civil, handled by the Sección de Inscripciones (Unidad de Matrimonios).

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: the two applicants (contrayentes) must present themselves together and both sign the request for the celebration of the civil marriage.

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: foreign applicants must provide the original and a legible copy of their identity document issued by the Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería, or their passport, valid and in good condition.

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: foreign applicants must provide a birth certificate from their country of origin, apostilled, and if it is in a language other than Spanish, with an official translation. It has no expiry, except where it is not in good condition or contains a correction to substantial data affecting identity.

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: foreign applicants must provide a civil status certificate, apostilled, and if it is in a language other than Spanish, with an official translation. It is valid for the period it expressly states; if none is stated, it must have been issued no more than one month before it is presented.

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: the applicants must supply details of the two people who will act as witnesses: full name and identity document number, phone and email, exact address, profession or occupation, and current civil status. A foreign witness must attach a complete copy of their document and send it to the Unidad de Matrimonios email address.

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: on the day, the two witnesses named in the request must attend with a valid identity document (for foreigners: passport, DIMEX or another official document issued by the Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería, or Foreign Ministry diplomatic or international mission cards), be sworn in during the ceremony, and know that the couple are free to marry with no legal impediment. Witnesses attend only on the day of the ceremony.

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: an edict (notice) must be published in the official gazette, Diario Oficial La Gaceta, through the Imprenta Nacional platform; the applicants must handle the quotation and bear the cost of publishing the edict.

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: to start the procedure the applicants must give an email address for notifications and a mobile phone number. On the day of the marriage the couple and witnesses must attend with their valid identity documents in good condition.

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: requests are received at the central office (Unidad de Matrimonios) Monday to Friday 7:00 to 10:00 am with 10 places per day, and at regional offices nationwide 7:00 am to 2:00 pm. Marriages are celebrated by appointment, Monday to Friday between 7:00 am and 2:00 pm, at the central office or the respective regional office.

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: the average time for this procedure is 4 to 6 months, depending on diary availability once the request and requirements are complete and the edict has been published.

As at November 2026, the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones (TSE) Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Celebración de Matrimonio Civil' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: the Registro Civil states this service (celebration of civil marriage before the Registro Civil) is free of charge ('Este servicio es gratuito'). The separate cost of publishing the edict is borne by the applicants (see fact_08).

As at November 2026, the TSE Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Inscripción de Matrimonio Civil o Católico' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: this is the procedure to register marriages celebrated in Costa Rican territory (at notarial offices, parishes or consular offices).

As at November 2026, the TSE Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Inscripción de Matrimonio Civil o Católico' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: the celebrating authority must complete, sign and seal the marriage declaration certificate supplied by the Sección de Inscripciones; for marriages celebrated before notaries, registration must use the digital marriage platform ('Matrimonio digital'), and the notary must have an enabled user in that system before the ceremony.

As at November 2026, the TSE Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Inscripción de Matrimonio Civil o Católico' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: for civil marriages where one or both parties are foreign, a certified copy of the valid identity document in good condition must also be provided with the marriage declaration.

As at November 2026, the TSE Registro Civil procedure sheet 'Inscripción de Matrimonio Civil o Católico' (tse.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: registration of a marriage between a Costa Rican and a foreigner, or between foreigners, takes 25 working days from receipt at the Sección de Inscripciones, as it involves a study verifying the identity of the foreign party (8 to 15 working days between Costa Ricans). The registration service is stated to be free.

As at November 2026, the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y Culto, Departamento de Autenticaciones page (rree.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: documents that arrive apostilled from abroad do not require any further approval from the Ministry to be recognised in Costa Rica. Documents in a language other than Spanish need an official translator, found through the Ministry's website, and that translation does not need to be authenticated.

As at November 2026, the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y Culto, Departamento de Autenticaciones page (rree.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: a public document issued in another State has no effect in Costa Rica unless it has been legalised by the Ministry or apostilled in the issuing State. The Apostille certifies only the authenticity of the signature, the capacity of the signatory and the seal, not the content of the document.

As at November 2026, the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y Culto, Departamento de Autenticaciones page (rree.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: all Costa Rican public documents that are to have legal effect in another State must be authenticated; for a country party to the Hague Apostille Convention the person obtains an Apostille attached to the physical document, which is also digitised for online verification. Documents issued by the Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones and documents made before a Notario Público are among the documents the department authenticates.

As at November 2026, the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y Culto, Departamento de Autenticaciones page (rree.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: the Departamento de Autenticaciones in San José works by appointment only, Monday to Friday; the procedure is not personal, so a third party can lodge documents without authorisation; documents are returned within 1 to 10 working days.

As at November 2026, the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y Culto page 'Requisitos para autenticar / apostillar' (rree.go.cr, read in full 17 November 2026; translated from Spanish) states: every document must show the public institution and the name of the public official who signs it, and the signature must be handwritten. Appointments are booked online.

Snippet only (search result, not read in full; translated from Spanish): the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y Culto appointment page for authentications states that for each document legalised or apostilled the law requires payment of a stamp (timbre). A fee applies; amount not recorded.

Snippet only (search result, not read in full; translated from Spanish): the TSE notary manual 'Matrimonio Civil Digital' indicates that where a party is foreign the notary selects 'extranjero' as nationality and enters all of that party's details in the system.

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need a CNI, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it also needs an authentication or apostille. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (last updated 18/08/2026, read live 12 November 2026): some countries ask you to prove you aren't already married; the most common documents are a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages; the country may have more rules (for example a residence period); 'We can't tell you what you will need'; contact your destination's embassy or consulate. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (read live 12 November 2026): your registry of births, deaths and marriages can give a statement that there's no record you have been married before, a Single Status certificate or a No Record Result certificate; local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, the death certificate of a deceased spouse, and your original birth certificate and passport.

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (read live 12 November 2026): Australia doesn't recognise overseas marriages where one or both people are already married to someone else, not old enough to get married, too closely related, or forced to get married.

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if, when it took place, it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia. A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage but may not work as proof of a name change (check with your local registry of births, deaths and marriages), and Smartraveller suggests talking to a lawyer to confirm the certificate is valid in Australia. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack, same source and date.] As at November 2026, the Attorney-General's Department (read live 12 November 2026): if Australia recognises your overseas marriage, you can't get married again in Australia, but you may choose to hold another type of ceremony, such as a confirmation of vows or a recommitment ceremony.

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller (DFAT), 'How to get your documents legalised' (last updated 30/09/2026): ask the overseas authority which documents they need and which must be legalised; DFAT 'can't tell you what they may want'. Find out from the intended authority or legal representative whether you need an apostille or an authentication certificate.

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller: documents that are not original Australian public documents must first be notarised by an Australian Notary Public; the apostille or authentication certificate is applied directly to the document, so if you don't want originals marked, get a notarised copy legalised (and check the overseas authority accepts it).

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller: requests use the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness, and can be lodged by appointment at an Australian Passport Office, in person at many Australian embassies, high commissions and consulates overseas (not Honorary Consul consulates), or by registered mail to the Authentications Section in Melbourne or Sydney. A fee applies (amount not recorded).

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller: processing times vary, with delays at the end of the school year and in peak holiday periods, for incomplete requests or unpaid fees, or when the issuing authority must be contacted. An Australian-issued apostille can be verified online via DFAT.

insider_details.detail: Order the single-status document last. Costa Rica's Registro Civil accepts a civil status certificate only for the period it states or, if none, for one month from issue, and it must be apostilled and officially translated into Spanish. Time the request so it is still current on lodgement day.

Build in real lead time. For a marriage before the Registro Civil, the TSE gives an average of 4 to 6 months, including publishing a notice in La Gaceta, and registration involving foreigners takes a further 25 working days.

Plan for two witnesses who can be present in person on the day with valid ID; foreign witnesses' documents are sent ahead by email. If guests are flying in, choose witnesses whose passport details can be supplied early.
Registro Civil ceremonies run by appointment on weekdays between 7am and 2pm, so a Saturday sunset ceremony is a celebration, not the legal step, unless another authorised route is confirmed.

For use back home, the Costa Rican marriage certificate needs a Costa Rican Apostille from the Foreign Ministry in San José (appointment only, 1 to 10 working days), and a third party can lodge it for you.

Schedule guest arrivals and departures at San José airport in daylight and book transfers through the hotel or an established operator: Smartraveller advises daylight airport movements, official or hotel-arranged transport, and avoiding driving at night.

Build weather contingency into any date in the June to November window: Smartraveller names it the hurricane and rainy season, with possible flight cancellations and road disruption, so plan a covered ceremony option and a buffer day for guest travel.

Brief guests that beach swimming on both coasts can be dangerous (rip tides, no lifeguards, crocodiles reported on the Pacific Coast), so keep any beach welcome event to the sand unless local advice says otherwise.
Tell guests to bring US dollars or cards rather than Australian cash, and to check their insurance covers medical evacuation, as private care is expensive and serious cases may be evacuated.

Start Australian paperwork early: Smartraveller says DFAT can't tell you what the overseas authority will want, and legalisation processing slows at the end of the school year and in peak holidays, so confirm the Costa Rican document list first, then apostille.
